correctness.rationale: Exact all-n proof decomposes the rim quotient the binary cyclic polynomial ring into its two-adic primary and invertible factors, with correct hub coupling. Odd rims split into a two-bit swap and invertible rim; even rims have the exact cubic-iterate cancellation identity and an explicitly proved rank sequence. Gcd kernels yield all-time point counts, and Möbius inversion gives primitive orbits. Newly executed standalone verify.py matched 1195 independent ranks, 1160 temporal fixed-point counts, and every labelled state for rim sizes from 3 to 10; finite tests corroborate but do not replace proof.

value.rationale: The graph family is the natural hub-joined cycle, and the precise XOR dynamics is the classic additive-graph rule. A nontrivial sharp 2-adic transient-depth transition, complete extinction for powers-of-two rim lengths, and all-time cycle/basin enumeration give structural information not supplied by generic reversible/irreversible tests or a fixed small graph computation. The results cover infinitely many graphs, with full exact recurrence and transient distribution.
